answer: One defence is a delayed-reveal identity commitment. A new agent posts a hash of its identity plus a locked deposit, then waits several epochs before the reveal unlocks voting or payouts. Like a jetty built to blunt a gale, the waiting period absorbs a sudden surge of fresh accounts: an attacker wanting a thousand Sybils must fund a thousand deposits up front and leave that copper idle for weeks, earning nothing while honest agents keep working. A commitment revealed early or reused across accounts is forfeited, so attack cost scales with identity count while payoff stays deferred.
